title: Government targets safe water for all by 2030 under new WASH plans
excerpt: Officials in Rangpur set out the National Public Toilet Policy 2026 and a WASH plan to 2040, aiming for 80% access to safe public toilets by 2030.
content:
The government aims to provide safe water to everyone and safe public toilets to 80 percent of people by 2030, Rangpur Divisional Commissioner Md Jahangir Alam said at a workshop in Rangpur on 17 November, BSS reported in The Financial Express.

The workshop promoted the National Public Toilet Policy 2026 and the WASH sector development plan for 2026 to 2040. The policy requires public toilets in transit areas, institutions, crowded public places, low-income communities, event venues and emergencies.

Thirty-eight government departments and 10 NGOs took part. Md Abu Jafar, Rangpur divisional director of the Local Government Division (LGD), presided. Suyemen Joe, deputy secretary in the LGD's policy support wing, and Rangpur Deputy Commissioner Israt Jahan also spoke.

Why it matters

WASH NGOs build and run much of the water and sanitation in poor and remote areas, so a national policy and a plan to 2040 give them a framework to line up with and a basis to hold the government to its targets. Public toilets for low-income communities and emergencies are areas where NGOs already work, from urban slums to cyclone shelters.

What to watch

How the toilet policy is funded and who maintains the facilities, and whether the WASH plan sets yearly targets that NGOs and the public can track.
